rows.jp: 「あ、そうか」
rows.en: “Oh. Right.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, right."

rows.jp: 日射病にでもなったら大変だ。
rows.en: Heatstroke would be no laughing matter.

ghs.en: It'd be a big problem if we ended up with sunstroke.

rows.jp: 「夕方からまた再起動です」
rows.en: “I'll start up again in the evening.”

ghs.en: Misato: "I will begin again after dusk."

rows.jp: 「手伝いましょうか？」
rows.en: “Would you like me to help?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Can I help you then?"

rows.jp: 「ぺけくんの方が強いです」
rows.en: “You are stronger than I am, X.”

ghs.en: Misato: "You are so much stronger, Peke-kun."

rows.jp: 「はい？」
rows.en: “What?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What?"

rows.jp: 「ちゃんと心の整理して、自分のやること決めてるんですから」
rows.en: “You've sorted out your feelings and decided what you're going to do.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Because you organize your mind as proper, and you are set on what you want to do."
ghs.assessment: The phrase for sorting out one's feelings is rendered as ungrammatical English, obscuring the praise that the addressee has done so properly.
ghs.remedy: Use idiomatic language for sorting out one's feelings and deciding what to do.

highlights.text: organize your mind as proper

rows.jp: 唐突に話が戻ったらしい。
rows.en: Apparently we're abruptly back to that subject.

ghs.en: Seems that subject has returned all of a sudden.
ghs.assessment: The narration says that the conversation has apparently returned to its earlier topic; the English is grammatically incomplete and treats the subject itself as an agent.
ghs.remedy: State idiomatically that she has suddenly returned to the earlier subject.

highlights.text: Seems that subject has returned

rows.jp: 「そりゃ先輩も同じでは？」
rows.en: “Isn't the same true of you?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, isn't it the same for you, Senpai?"

rows.jp: 瓜実型の輪郭に、仄かな憂いが訪れた。
rows.en: A trace of sorrow settles over her oval face.

ghs.en: An indistinct sadness came to that melon-shaped silhouette.
ghs.assessment: The fixed descriptor refers to an oval face or facial outline, not a melon-shaped silhouette; the mistranslation distorts the image and its object.
ghs.remedy: Describe the faint sadness crossing her oval face.

highlights.text: melon-shaped silhouette

rows.jp: 泣きそうなようにも見えて、胸を締めつけられる。
rows.en: She almost looks ready to cry, and my chest tightens.

ghs.en: Seeing something so as if to cry makes my chest tighten.
ghs.assessment: The source says that she looks almost ready to cry, which tightens the narrator's chest; the English removes that subject and is not grammatical.
ghs.remedy: Restore her as the apparent subject of crying and retain the narrator's reaction.

highlights.text: Seeing something so as if to cry

rows.jp: そうだ。
rows.en: That's right.

ghs.en: That's right.

rows.jp: 彼女だけが、俺をこんな気分にさせる。
rows.en: She alone can make me feel this way.

ghs.en: It is her alone who can make me feel that.

rows.jp: ありきたりで、当たり前の、胸を張って誇れる……想い。
rows.en: A perfectly ordinary, natural feeling—one I can hold my head high and be proud of.

ghs.en: That proud, conventional, ordinary puff of the chest... an emotion.
ghs.assessment: The source describes an ordinary, natural feeling one can openly take pride in; the rendering turns the idiom about holding one's chest high into a malformed noun phrase.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the sequence of ordinary, natural, and proudly avowable qualities as modifiers of the feeling.

highlights.text: proud, conventional, ordinary puff of the chest

rows.jp: 異性としての感情かどうかはさておき、俺はこの人が好きなんだと思う。
rows.en: Whether or not what I feel is romantic, I think I love her.

ghs.en: Even setting aside whether or not these feelings are caused by her being of opposite gender, I think I really like this person.
ghs.assessment: The clause asks whether the feeling is attraction toward her as a member of the opposite sex; it does not frame her gender as the mechanical cause of the feeling.
ghs.remedy: Use idiomatic language for setting aside whether the feeling is romantic or sexual attraction.

highlights.text: caused by her being of opposite gender

rows.jp: 幸せになってほしい。
rows.en: I want her to be happy.

ghs.en: I want her to be happy,

rows.jp: 嫌われたくない。
rows.en: I don't want her to hate me.

ghs.en: I don't want to be hated by her.

rows.jp: 「どうかしましたか？」
rows.en: “Is something wrong?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Is there some problem?"

rows.jp: 「どわあっ！？」
rows.en: “Wagh!?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "d'Wah?!"

rows.jp: 眼前に先輩の顔がアップで迫っていた。
rows.en: Mimi's face suddenly fills my vision.

ghs.en: Senpai upped the level of proximity of her face to right under my nose.
ghs.assessment: The narration presents her face looming close before his eyes; the rendering mechanically expands 'close-up' into an unnatural abstraction.
ghs.remedy: State directly that her face had suddenly loomed close before him.

highlights.text: upped the level of proximity of her face

rows.jp: 「わっ？」
rows.en: “Wah?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Wah?"

rows.jp: 「べっくらこきました」
rows.en: “You flabberstarted me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was scary'd!"
ghs.assessment: The comic dialectal expression means that he was startled or surprised; the invented form instead suggests that he frightened someone and is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use a playful or rustic-sounding form of 'I was surprised.'

highlights.text: scary'd

rows.jp: 「ふむ、べっくら……ふむ」
rows.en: “Hmm. ‘Flabberstarted’... Hmm.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Hum, scary'd... hum."
ghs.assessment: Her repetition is interest in the preceding dialectal word for surprise; repeating the mistranslated invention prevents the wordplay from functioning.
ghs.remedy: Repeat the same playful surprise-word used in the preceding line.

highlights.text: scary'd

rows.jp: なにやら感心している。
rows.en: She seems rather taken with it.

ghs.en: She is impressed by something.

rows.jp: 「暑くなってきたし、校舎に戻りません？」
rows.en: “It's getting hot. Want to head back inside?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It is getting hotter, will you not go back inside the building?"
ghs.assessment: The negative question is an inclusive suggestion to return to the school building, not a formal request for the other person alone to go back.
ghs.remedy: Use an inclusive suggestion such as 'shall we head back inside?'

highlights.text: will you not go back inside the building

rows.jp: 「そうしますか」
rows.en: “Let’s do that.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Yes, I should."
ghs.assessment: The response accepts a shared plan, whereas the rendering changes it to a statement about what the speaker individually ought to do.
ghs.remedy: Accept the shared suggestion with 'Let's do that' or equivalent.

highlights.text: I should

rows.jp: 放送部の部長さんは、一度だけアンテナに視線を移した。
rows.en: The president of the Broadcasting Club glances once at the antenna.

ghs.en: The President of the Broadcast Club moved her sight to the antenna, only once.
ghs.assessment: The action is a single glance toward the antenna; 'moved her sight' and the displaced modifier are mechanical rather than idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: State directly that she glanced at the antenna once.

highlights.text: moved her sight to the antenna, only once

ghs.en: Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: なにを思っているのかはわからない。
rows.en: I have no idea what she is thinking.

ghs.en: What she's thinking I don't know.

rows.jp: この人は、そうたやすく本心を見せたりはしない。
rows.en: She doesn't show her true feelings easily.

ghs.en: This person here does not want to show her true feelings all that easily.
ghs.assessment: The source says she does not readily reveal her true feelings; the rendering adds an explicit desire not to reveal them.
ghs.remedy: Describe her habitual reluctance or reserve without adding a stated intention.

highlights.text: does not want to show

rows.jp: だからこそ、さっきの唖然とした顔は貴重なのであり。
rows.en: That makes the stunned face I saw earlier all the more precious.

ghs.en: That is exactly why the face of mute displeasure she made earlier is so precious.
ghs.assessment: The adjective describes a stunned or dumbfounded expression, not mute displeasure; the emotional content is changed.
ghs.remedy: Describe the earlier face as stunned or dumbfounded.

highlights.text: mute displeasure

rows.jp: 柔和な顔は仮面でしかないんだと、俺はわかってしまうのだ。
rows.en: And why I find myself believing that her gentle face is only a mask.

ghs.en: Her gentle face is nothing but a mask, this I completely understand.
ghs.assessment: The underlying realization is retained, but the comma splice and fronted demonstrative produce unidiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Integrate the realization as a normal subordinate clause.

highlights.text: mask, this
